Kevin Trudeau put out one wish: $100,000 a week, with no idea how.

A week later, in a New York deli, the stranger at the next table recognized him back. That stranger ran TV infomercials — and so did the next guy who called that same night.

Within weeks his memory course was on air. $450 million in sales. His first week's royalty check alone topped $290,000.

One wish, one sandwich, one phone call — and a check nobody could have planned for.

Kevin Trudeau says there are exactly three reasons the law of attraction fails for most people.

First, people skip steps in the manifesting formula. Second, they carry counter intentions buried in their own DNA. Third, their brain broadcasts on the wrong wave.

Poor people broadcast mostly on beta. Rich people broadcast between alpha and theta — what Kevin calls the wealth wave.

Fix those three, and the law of attraction can finally work.

Andrew Carnegie sold his steel company for the equivalent of $400 billion in cash — more real cash than Elon Musk or Jeff Bezos have today, since theirs is mostly stock.

He gave almost all of it away and built libraries across America. Then he paid Napoleon Hill to interview the richest men alive and write down how they think.

Henry Ford objected: if regular people learned to think this way, who would work in his factories?

Kevin Trudeau's answer — that's exactly why the real methods stay hidden from the average person.

clips.end_words: I can always refill the glass
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau once asked General Norman Schwartzkopf what happens when his army retreats.

"We never retreat," the general said. "We regroup." Same situation, completely different mindset.

Millionaires use the same trick with money. Ask a wealthy person if the glass is half empty or half full, Kevin says, and they'll tell you it doesn't matter — you can always refill the glass.

Reframing isn't denial. It's how rich people stay in motion instead of getting stuck.
